name: Ana Mendieta
bio: Ana Mendieta (1948–1985) was born in Havana, Cuba. In 1961, aged 12, she was exiled to the United States with her sister and separated from her parents, brother and homeland. She studied art and archaeology at the University of Iowa, where she developed her practice on the experimental Intermedia programme between 1972 and 1977. She made her first Silueta in Mexico in 1973 (Imágen de Yágul) and went on to burn, carve and mould life-size traces of her body into landscapes with earth, fire, blood, flowers and water, works she called 'earth-body' art. Because these works were ephemeral, she recorded them in photographs and in more than 100 films and videos, many shot on Super 8. She also made early performance works such as Untitled (Rape Scene) and Moffitt Building Piece, both 1973, in response to violence against women. In 1981 she returned to Cuba to carve the Esculturas Rupestres (Rupestrian Sculptures) into limestone, and after winning the Rome Prize in 1983 she turned to studio sculpture at the American Academy in Rome before her death in New York in 1985.
studyNotes: The body is the unit of measure. In Body Tracks and across the Siluetas, the size of the figure is set by her own reach and height. One rule (my body, life-size) generated a whole decade of work in very different places.

Material carries the meaning. Earth, fire (Alma, Silueta en Fuego), gunpowder, blood, feathers, flowers and water each change what the same outline says. Try keeping the form fixed and changing only the material.

The documentation is the artwork. The actions were ephemeral and left to erode, so the photograph or film is what survives. She made deliberate choices about the print, the slide and the film frame rather than treating them as neutral records.

Watch how the films are framed. A mostly static camera, often looking down at the ground, holds a single shot while the image burns, smokes, floods or breathes (Grass Breathing). The shot lasts as long as the process, and the body is often absent or hidden.

Return to a site. She went back to places that mattered to her (Old Man's Creek in Iowa, Oaxaca in Mexico, and Cuba for the Rupestrian Sculptures), so a location could hold a series. Choosing a site was part of the work.
A series that will never end. The Siluetas show how one simple motif repeated over years stays alive through variation in scale, material, season and medium: photograph, film, carved stone.

works.title: Grass Breathing
works.medium: Super-8mm film, shown as HD video, colour, silent, 3 min 8 s
works.note: A patch of turf rises and falls as she breathes beneath it, unseen.
works.collection: Tate, lent by the Tate Americas Foundation (L04622)
works.credit: © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Courtesy Marian Goodman Gallery (film still)

works.title: Untitled (Facial Hair Transplants)
works.note: She glued a classmate's beard hair onto her own face, testing how gender is read from the surface of the body.
works.credit: © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Courtesy Marian Goodman Gallery (installation view)

works.title: Imágen de Yágul
works.medium: C-print (printed 1991), from Silueta Works in Mexico 1973–77
works.note: She lay in an open tomb at the archaeological site of Yagul, Oaxaca, covered in white flowers. She later considered it the first Silueta.
works.credit: © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Courtesy Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London

works.title: Moffitt Building Piece
works.medium: 35mm colour slides (shown at Tate Modern as 16 inkjet prints)
works.note: She spilled animal blood on an Iowa City pavement and photographed passers-by from a parked car, recording how people walk past violence.
works.credit: © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Courtesy Marian Goodman Gallery

works.title: Body Tracks
works.medium: Super-8mm film transferred to HD, colour, silent, 1 min 1 s
works.note: With her hands and forearms dipped in blood and tempera, she slid down a white wall, leaving marks set by the reach of her own body.
works.credit: © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Courtesy Marian Goodman Gallery (film still)

works.title: Alma, Silueta en Fuego
works.medium: Super-8mm film, colour, silent, 3 min 7 s
works.note: A body-shaped outline burns on the ground until it is consumed. The camera holds still for the whole burn.
works.credit: © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Courtesy Marian Goodman Gallery (film still)

works.title: Untitled: Silueta Series
works.medium: Super-8mm film, shown as HD video, colour, silent, 3 min 14 s
works.credit: © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Courtesy Marian Goodman Gallery (film still)

works.title: Bacayu (Light of Day), from Esculturas Rupestres
works.medium: Gelatin silver print documenting a figure carved into limestone
works.note: Carved into a cave wall at Jaruco, Cuba, on her return after twenty years in exile.
